message.content:
Here’s a quick‑look list of the long‑weekend holidays that Canadians enjoyed in 2023.  
(“Long weekend” means a holiday that falls on a Friday or Monday, or a holiday that falls on a weekend but is observed on the following Monday, giving you a 3‑day break.)

| Holiday | Date in 2023 | Long‑Weekend Span |
|---------|--------------|-------------------|
| **New Year’s Day** | Jan 1 (Sunday) – observed Mon 2 | **Dec 30 – Jan 3** (Sat – Tue) |
| **Family Day** *(Alberta, BC, NB, NL, ON, PEI, SK, MB)* | Feb 20 (Monday) | **Feb 18 – Feb 20** (Sat – Mon) |
| **Good Friday** | Apr 7 (Friday) | **Apr 7 – Apr 9** (Fri – Sun) |
| **Victoria Day** | May 22 (Monday) | **May 20 – May 22** (Sat – Mon) |
| **Canada Day** | Jul 1 (Saturday) – observed Mon 3 | **Jul 1 – Jul 3** (Sat – Mon) |
| **Labour Day** | Sep 4 (Monday) | **Sep 2 – Sep 4** (Sat – Mon) |
| **Thanksgiving** | Oct 9 (Monday) | **Oct 7 – Oct 9** (Sat – Mon) |
| **Remembrance Day** | Nov 11 (Saturday) – observed Mon 13 | **Nov 11 – Nov 13** (Sat – Mon) |
| **Christmas Day** | Dec 25 (Monday) | **Dec 23 – Dec 25** (Sat – Mon) |

> **Quick note:**  
> • Family Day is a statutory holiday in several provinces (not nationwide).  
> • Boxing Day (Dec 26 Tuesday) does not create a long weekend in 2023.  

Feel free to plug these dates straight into your holiday‑planning app!
